findings.title: Item write paths unconditionally reset subject_keys shredded state; post-erasure write protection rests entirely on the KMS
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/envelope_persist.rs:38-47 (SQLite) and :80-89 (Postgres): the legacy `put_item` upsert sets `status = 'active', shredded_at = NULL` on conflict, unconditionally and before the items upsert. The same reset exists on the gated-create path: crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_memory.rs:157-167 and crates/clio-store/src/postgres_memory.rs:126-136. Compliance erasure (crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_erase.rs:140-156, postgres_erase.rs parity) marks the row `status='shredded'` and destroys the DEK via the KMS. The only thing that stops a write to an erased subject is `DekProvider::ensure_dek` failing with `ErasedSubject` — implemented only by `LocalDevKms` (crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs:163-167, 223-235). The `DekProvider` contract itself (dek.rs:87-114) does not require `ensure_dek` to reject a previously-destroyed subject; any alternate or remote provider that re-issues a key for a subject (or whose destroyed-state bookkeeping diverges from the store's `subject_keys` row) lets `put_item` / `create_memory_item` reactivate the subject_keys row and re-seal new content for an erased subject. Exploit condition: a non-LocalDevKms `DekProvider` implementation, or state divergence between the KMS key store and the database. With LocalDevKms the path is currently unreachable because ensure_dek fails first. Verification of the erasure happy path is solid: sqlite_erase.rs:141-147 probes that the key is really destroyed before writing the shredded row.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed in the store itself: inside `create_memory_item_tx` / `update_memory_item_tx` / the envelope upsert transactions, first read `subject_keys.status`/`shredded_at` for the target subject and reject `ErasedSubject` when shredded, instead of resetting `shredded_at = NULL` on every write. Keep the KMS check as the second layer.

resolution.how: Every `subject_keys` upsert in the codebase (14 sites across 12 files, both backends) now keeps `shredded_at` set: the conflict update carries `WHERE subject_keys.shredded_at IS NULL`, and a suppressed update (0 affected rows) is mapped to a named `ErrorCode::ErasedSubject` error (`shredded_subject_err` / `check_subject_reactivation` in crates/clio-store/src/item_persist.rs). The guard is a defense-in-depth backstop: with a fail-closed provider the KMS already refuses before the upsert; with a provider that resurrects keys, the storage layer now refuses to reactivate the subject. No compliant flow changes: with LocalDevKms, writes for destroyed DEKs failed before the upsert already.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/subject_shred_guard_tests.rs: a `FailOpenKms` double that passes the erase-time destruction probe once and then resurrects keys; `sqlite_fail_open_kms_cannot_reactivate_shredded_subject` and `pg_fail_open_kms_cannot_reactivate_shredded_subject` both assert `ErasedSubject` on post-erase writes and that the `shredded` marker survives. Guard sites: belief_tx.rs, envelope_persist.rs, postgres_correct.rs, postgres_history_write.rs, postgres_memory.rs, postgres_persona.rs, postgres_triple.rs, sqlite_correct.rs, sqlite_history_write.rs, sqlite_memory.rs, sqlite_persona.rs, sqlite_triple.rs.

findings.title: Template-provider extraction egresses source_text and tool_payload without the secret scrubbing the hosted path applies
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs:225-233: `TemplateApiExtractor::extract` puts `req.source_text` and `req.tool_payload` into the request body verbatim. The hosted chat adapter scrubs both: crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:84-87 (`masked_clone` + `scrub_inline_secrets` on the tool payload) and :113-117 (inline-secret scrub on source text). `build_extractor_from` (crates/clio-write/src/extract_factory.rs:70-76) accepts provider `""`/`"template"` with any configured `extract.url` — nothing restricts the endpoint to a local sidecar and no build-time URL validation runs for this branch (the `openai` branch does validate via `ChatExtractor::new`, extract_chat.rs:240-269). Exploit condition: a deployment configures `extract.provider = template` (or leaves it empty) pointing at a remote URL; memory content containing inline `key: secret` pairs then leaves the process unmasked, while the identical content via `provider = openai` would be scrubbed. The module doc for extract_chat.rs:11-20 declares the scrubbed egress as the intended contract, so the template path is a silent inconsistency, not a documented trade-off.
findings.requirement_ref: extract_chat.rs module contract (secret-scrubbed egress) and §4.9.5.A secret-protection rule in spirit
findings.recommendation: Apply the same `masked_clone` + `scrub_inline_secrets` treatment to the template request body (a shared `scrub_payload` helper), or fail closed at factory build time when provider is template and `extract.url` is not a loopback/local address. Security-relevant.

resolution.how: Chose the scrubbing option (the URL restriction would break the documented no-egress default template deployment). `TemplateApiExtractor::extract` now scrubs inline `key: secret` pairs from `source_text`, applies `masked_clone` to `tool_payload`, and scrubs `verify_feedback` before building the request body — the same `clio_config::secret` scrubbers the chat path uses.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs (template egress block); `extract::extract_tests::template_egress_is_scrubbed_like_chat_path` asserts the captured request body contains no raw secret while non-secret payload fields survive.

findings.title: Cross-bank item id collision on legacy put_item and opaque-item upserts silently reports success
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/envelope_persist.rs:48-64 (SQLite) and :90-107 (Postgres): the items upsert carries `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ... WHERE items.bank_id = excluded.bank_id`, and the affected-row count is ignored (`conn.execute(...).am(...)?` discards it). When the id already exists under a different bank, the guarded UPDATE matches 0 rows, the statement succeeds, and `put_item` returns `Ok(())` while nothing was written. I reproduced the SQL semantics directly with Python/sqlite3 (same statement shape): result is rowcount 0, no error, original row untouched. The identical pattern exists in crates/clio-store/src/opaque_item_persist.rs:35-87 and :94-146, which the batch executors use for `BatchWrite::PutOpaqueItem` (crates/clio-store/src/batch_sqlite.rs:224, batch_postgres.rs:226) — i.e. a sync/apply or batch write whose id collides across banks is silently dropped and reported applied. Contrast: the memory-item create path checks row counts (`map_item_insert`, item_persist.rs:103-124) and the update path errors on 0 rows (item_update.rs:80-85), so this is specific to the envelope and opaque upserts. Impact: silent divergence between peers (the sync convergence rule assumes applied writes actually landed) and silent success on a caller error (wrong bank).
findings.requirement_ref: §4.9.5.D sync convergence rule (already-admitted applies MUST land); general correctness (AGENTS.md: do the work properly)
findings.recommendation: Capture the affected-row count in both `envelope_row_*` and `put_opaque_item_*_tx` helpers and return a structured error (e.g. InvalidArgument 'item id exists in another bank') when it is 0, matching the update path's behavior.

resolution.how: `envelope_row_sqlite`/`envelope_row_postgres` and `put_opaque_item_sqlite_tx`/`put_opaque_item_postgres_tx` now capture the affected-row count and return the named `InvalidArgument` error `cross_bank_item_err` (`check_item_upsert_applied` in crates/clio-store/src/item_persist.rs) when the same-bank guard suppresses the upsert. Same-bank re-put remains an idempotent update.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/memory_item_tests.rs `suite_legacy_put_item` (runs for SQLite and Postgres via `run_memory_suite`): cross-bank put_item errors, original row untouched, same-bank re-put still succeeds.

findings.title: No CI exercise of the extraction pipeline against a real extraction model; verification claims rest on fixtures and stub transports
findings.evidence: Every pipeline/ingest test drives extraction with `FixtureExtractor` or `PoisonExtractor` (crates/clio-write/src/ingest_tests.rs:97,144,203-214; ingest_leaf_tests.rs:156,205,245,285,325; ingest_gate_tests.rs:80,143; pipeline_tests.rs:225; raw_ingest_tests.rs:60-72). The real `HttpTransport` is exercised exactly once, against a hand-rolled one-response TCP server (raw_ingest_tests.rs:130-150 `config_resolved_extractor_runs_over_http`); the only other live-transport tests assert failure against a closed port (extract_chat_tests.rs:263-282). `ChatExtractor` is otherwise tested only through stub `Transport` impls (extract_chat_tests.rs:255-261, 311-325). No test or CI workflow runs a real NuExtract sidecar or a hosted chat model: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the Makefile contain no extract/sidecar target. Consequence: real-model behavior — the actual NuExtract response shape, chat-model compliance with SYSTEM_PROMPT (verbatim values, no fences), real provider error bodies, and `source_ref`/`diagnostic` semantics — is never exercised, so 'extraction + span verification works' is proven only for the harness stubs. The fail-closed pipeline design (pipeline.rs:198-240: verify → retry once with feedback → refuse, no write) bounds the blast radius, but systematic extractor-side failures (e.g. a model that systematically paraphrases) would surface only as 100% refusal in production, unmeasured.
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md Core Principles (Be honest / Verify your work) and the Coverage Gate's intent that reported paths are exercised
findings.recommendation: Add an opt-in, non-CI integration target (documented manual gate or nightly job) that runs `ingest_raw` against a local NuExtract sidecar with a fixed transcript corpus and asserts admit/refuse rates and snapshot shapes; record in the phase documentation that CI coverage of extraction is stub-level only until that exists.

resolution.how: Accepted as a documented limitation. Adding a live-model integration target (sidecar-driven nightly job with admit/refuse-rate assertions) is CI/ops infrastructure outside this phase's scope; building a fixture-based stand-in would not address the finding. Recorded as a known limitation with no assigned owner; a follow-up needs an operator decision on where live-model gates live (CI vs documented manual gate).
resolution.evidence: This disposition; the compose stack already runs a NuExtract-class sidecar locally (docker compose `extract` service), so the opt-in target is feasible but deliberately deferred.

findings.title: Ungated update_memory_item primitive permits re-pointing an item to a different subject (DEK-domain move) with no boundary check
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:52-79 / :120-146: the UPDATE sets `subject_id` from the item and the caller re-seals content under the new subject's DEK before calling (sqlite_memory.rs:264-279). There is no check that the subject is unchanged or that the actor is authorized to move the item across subjects. Consequence: an item can be moved out of a subject's erasure scope — a subsequent `erase_request` on the old subject (which selects rows by subject_id, sqlite_erase.rs:102,131) would no longer cover the item, and its content now decrypts under the new subject's key. Scope honesty: I found no MCP/CLI tool that exposes arbitrary subject re-pointing on update today — `summarize_tools.rs:243-249` clones the existing item (same subject) and `clio-sync/src/apply.rs:226` applies the remote revision as-is — so this is reachable only through direct library use of the public trait method. The gate-boundary tripwire (gate_boundary_tests.rs) also does not cover `update_memory_item(`.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-19 / §7.4 (erasure scope by subject), FR-10 (no write path bypasses tool gating)
findings.recommendation: Either reject `item.subject_id != stored.subject_id` inside `update_memory_item_*_tx` (re-pointing is not a documented update use case), or document the cross-subject move as an explicit, audited operation. Add `update_memory_item(` to the gate-boundary scan. Security-relevant.

resolution.how: `update_memory_item_sqlite_tx` / `update_memory_item_postgres_tx` now read the stored subject inside the transaction and reject any subject change with the named `InvalidArgument` error `subject_immutable_err` (crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs, helper in item_persist.rs) — the subject anchors the DEK and erasure scope. Row-missing behavior is unchanged. The gate-boundary scan addition is handled under F-06's remediation.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/memory_item_tests.rs `suite_halves_update` (parity, both backends): moving an item to `other-subject` errors with 'cannot change subject_id'; same-subject updates still pass (the same suite revises the item beforehand).

findings.title: Admission gate-boundary tripwire has an uncovered bypass class (apply_batch / BatchWrite::CreateItem) and a stale allowlist entry
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/gate_boundary_tests.rs:60-89 scans only for the literal `create_memory_item(`. The batch executor offers an equally ungated create path — `BatchStore::apply_batch` with `BatchWrite::CreateItem` writes items with no admission re-check (crates/clio-store/src/batch_sqlite.rs:80-83, batch_postgres.rs:82, contract at batch_model.rs:215) — and a new caller of `apply_batch(&[BatchWrite::CreateItem{..}])` would pass the tripwire. Today's production callers do gate: MCP batch preflight scores every op through `gated_store_verified` before staging (crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:72-98), `canonical_put` scores through `gated_store_verified` (crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:181), `store_write` and `raw_ingest` persist only inside the gated write closure, and sync apply is the documented already-admitted exception. Also, the allowlist entry for `crates/clio-compliance/src/canonical.rs` (gate_boundary_tests.rs:39) is stale: that file no longer names `create_memory_item(` (it persists via `BatchWrite::CanonicalPut`), so the allowlist is broader than the code requires.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-10 (no memory admission decision bypasses tool gating); the tripwire's own stated purpose (gate_boundary_tests.rs:3-7)
findings.recommendation: Extend the scan to `apply_batch(` and `BatchWrite::CreateItem` occurrences outside the gate wrappers, and remove the stale canonical.rs allowlist entry. Low because current callers are verified to gate.

resolution.how: `gate_boundary_tests.rs` now runs a second source scan for `BatchWrite::CreateItem` with a documented allowlist (batch executors, compliance import already-admitted restore, MCP batch preflight/tools, test fixtures), and the stale `canonical.rs` entry was removed from the `create_memory_item` allowlist after verifying that file no longer names the primitive.
resolution.evidence: `only_gated_path_creates_items` and the new `batch_create_items_only_through_documented_paths` both pass against the current tree.

findings.title: Template-provider response parsing and build-time validation are weaker than the chat path
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/extract.rs:235: `TemplateApiExtractor` accepts `snapshot` as any non-null JSON value (`resp.get("snapshot").cloned().filter(|v| !v.is_null())`), whereas `parse_chat_response` requires an object and fails closed on other shapes (extract_chat.rs:195-199). A misbehaving sidecar returning a string/array snapshot flows into `verify_snapshot`, which fails closed on lookups (pipeline.rs:146-150), so the impact is confusing refusal diagnostics rather than ungrounded admission. Additionally, `build_extractor_from` constructs `TemplateApiExtractor` without any URL/model validation (extract_factory.rs:70-76) — an empty or malformed `extract.url` surfaces only as a per-request transport error, while the `openai` branch fails closed at build time (extract_factory.rs:77-91).
findings.requirement_ref: extract_factory.rs documented fail-closed rules (extract_factory.rs:40-45); consistency with parse_chat_response contract
findings.recommendation: Validate `snapshot.is_object()` in the template response parser (mirroring parse_chat_response) and run the same empty-url/model checks for the template branch at factory build time.

resolution.how: Snapshot shape: `TemplateApiExtractor` now requires a JSON object (or absent/null) for `snapshot` and fails closed with a named error on other shapes, mirroring `parse_chat_response`. Build-time URL/model validation: ACCEPTED AS DESIGNED rather than added — an empty `extract.url` with the template provider is the documented no-egress default (`t34_09_default_is_template_without_egress` in extract_factory_tests.rs) and the FR-28 readiness contract (`clio-mcp/src/runtime_open.rs::extract_available_from`) deliberately defines the template provider as needing only a URL; adding model validation would contradict that contract. Recorded here so the asymmetry is a decision, not an oversight.
resolution.evidence: `extract::extract_tests::template_rejects_non_object_snapshot`; factory test `t34_09_default_is_template_without_egress` unchanged and still passing, documenting the intentional empty-URL template default.

scope_notes: Phase 003 (memory-item core): I read item_persist.rs, envelope_persist.rs, opaque_item_persist.rs, sqlite_store.rs, postgres_store.rs, store.rs (Store trait), sqlite_memory.rs, postgres_memory.rs (create/update tx bodies), item_update.rs, dek.rs (DEK lifecycle + CiphertextEnvelope), sqlite_erase.rs, batch_sqlite.rs, gate_boundary_tests.rs, and the callers of the ungated primitives (clio-mcp store_write.rs, batch_preflight.rs, additive_tools.rs, summarize_tools.rs, clio-write raw_ingest.rs, hub_distill.rs, clio-sync apply.rs). Judged sound: legacy put_item rows fail closed on the typed read path (get_memory_item/get_snapshot/get_gist map to content_format_mismatch, item_persist.rs:42-53, 83-89) and there is no plaintext decrypt fallback anywhere (get_item requires a parseable CiphertextEnvelope and a matching, non-destroyed DEK version, sqlite_store.rs:55-90, dek.rs:263-308); duplicate ids and empty actors are rejected on create; updates require an existing row (row-count checked, item_update.rs:80-85) and stamp audit rows plus index enqueues inside the same transaction; the erasure transaction probes that the DEK is truly destroyed before writing the shredded subject_keys row (sqlite_erase.rs:140-147); the admission tripwire's allowlisted callers were each verified to actually route through gated_create/gated_store_verified or the documented already-admitted sync exception. Findings F-01, F-03, F-05, F-06 cover what is not sound. Phase 005 (online extraction + span verification): I read extract.rs, extract_chat.rs, extract_factory.rs, pipeline.rs, store_path.rs, verify.rs, raw_ingest.rs and their test files, plus .github/workflows/ci.yml and the Makefile. Judged sound: the extract → verify → retry-once → refuse loop never writes on refusal and retains only gist/diagnostic (pipeline.rs:194-240); gated_store_verified re-runs span verify before admission and requires source_text whenever a snapshot is present (store_path.rs:161-223); snapshot-less store-tool items skip span verify by design, which matches the requirement text (verification is conditional on snapshot presence); chat response parsing is strictly fail-closed (fences never stripped, provider error bodies bounded and scrubbed, oversized content rejected, extract_chat.rs:157-217); the user message neutralizes delimiter tags against prompt breakout and masks tool payloads (extract_chat.rs:72-126); endpoint URL assembly tolerates base variants and rejects bad schemes. The gap the parent flagged is partially accurate: CI is not strictly fixtures-only (one raw_ingest test drives the real HttpTransport against a fake HTTP server, and live-transport failure paths are tested), but no test anywhere runs a real extraction model, which is finding F-04. Findings F-02 and F-07 cover the template-provider asymmetries. I did not run the full test gate or coverage tooling (out of scope per instructions); the only runtime evidence I produced was the sqlite3/Python upsert-semantics repro backing F-03. I could not fully verify F-01's exploit condition at runtime because it requires a non-LocalDevKms DekProvider implementation; the finding is based on the trait contract (dek.rs:87-114) not requiring the fail-closed behavior LocalDevKms happens to provide.
dispositions_note: All security-tagged findings (F-01, F-02, F-05) and all correctness findings (F-03, F-06, F-07 snapshot shape) are remedied and tested. F-04 is the single accepted risk (live-model CI infrastructure, out of scope, no owner assigned). F-07's build-time url/model validation was accepted as designed behavior (documented no-egress template default + FR-28 readiness contract); the snapshot-shape gap is remedied.
